lessons.title: Why does a helmet need proper care?
lessons.summary: Identify the helmet’s three areas and choose the right care method for each.

content.text: Why a helmet needs careful attention

While riding, insects, road dust and rain collect on the helmet, while its interior is exposed to sweat and moisture. Dirt on the outside of the visor can reduce visibility, and neglected padding can make the helmet less comfortable. When speaking with a customer, first find out which part of the helmet needs attention.
Three areas, three care methods
Shell and outer visor
For dried-on insects, do not start by rubbing the surface dry. Helmet Gel softens the dirt so it can be gently wiped away. Helmet Detailer is used afterwards to finish the already-clean surface.
Lining

A freshener helps keep the lining fresh between washes, but it does not remove dirt like washing does. Before washing, check whether the lining can be removed and follow the helmet’s care instructions.
Pinlock

The Pinlock insert is delicate and must be treated separately. Do not apply gel or detailer to it, and do not rub it. Rinse it with distilled water and leave it to air-dry, following the helmet manufacturer’s recommendations.
How to start the conversation
Ask whether the customer wants to care for the visor and shell, the interior, or both. Then recommend a product. Do not assume that everyone needs a complete kit or daily care.

product_bullets: Treat the shell, outer visor and lining separately—each area requires a different approach.
First soften dried-on insects with Helmet Gel; do not rub them off dry.
Use Helmet Detailer to finish a clean surface.
An interior freshener does not replace washing a dirty lining.
Treat the Pinlock insert separately and follow the helmet manufacturer’s instructions.

conversation.text: I have a new helmet. Do I need to buy the complete care kit straight away?
conversation.speaker: client

conversation.text: No. If you want to care for the visor and shell now, choose products for the outer surfaces. An interior product is only useful when the lining needs freshening up or washing.
conversation.speaker: seller

conversation.text: Can I use one liquid to clean both the visor and the interior?
conversation.speaker: client

conversation.text: It is better to treat these as separate steps. Use products intended for visors on the outside, and clean the lining with a separate product according to the helmet instructions.
conversation.speaker: seller

conversation.text: For now, the only problem is insects on the visor.
conversation.speaker: client

conversation.text: In that case, start with Helmet Gel and a clean microfibre cloth. You can add the Detailer if you also want to finish the clean visor.
conversation.speaker: seller

lessons.title: Helmet Gel and Helmet Detailer: the difference and how to use them
lessons.summary: Learn the correct order for using Helmet Gel and Helmet Detailer, and choose the cloth and product size to suit the customer’s needs.

content.text: Two products, two different functions
Helmet Gel and Helmet Detailer work together, but neither replaces the other. The gel prepares a dirty surface, while the Detailer is used after it has been cleaned.
Step 1: Soften the dirt

Apply Helmet Gel to the dirty area and leave it for the time stated on the label. The travel size specifies about five minutes; shorten the time in strong sunlight. Do not let the product dry. Once the dirt has softened, wipe it away with a clean microfibre cloth without pressing hard.
Step 2: Finish the clean surface
Use Helmet Detailer only after removing the dirt. A thicker microfibre cloth works well for wiping away loosened dirt; use an Evolon cloth for the final finish. Always start with clean accessories.
Choose the size to suit how it will be used
The 30 ml size is easy to take on a trip. The 250 ml bottle is practical for regular helmet cleaning. Ask the customer where and how often they plan to use the products.

product_bullets: Helmet Gel is step 1: it softens dried-on insects and dirt so you can remove them gently.
After applying, wait as directed; the travel size specifies about 5 minutes. Shorten the wait in direct sunlight.
Helmet Detailer is step 2: use it on a clean surface for an even finish and to help prevent streaks.
Wipe away loosened dirt with a clean, thicker microfibre cloth; use Evolon for the final finish.
The products are available in a 30 ml travel size and a larger 250 ml size. Choose according to how often they will be used.

conversation.text: Is the Detailer alone enough for dried-on insects?
conversation.speaker: client

conversation.text: For dried-on insects, start with Helmet Gel: soften the dirt, gently wipe it away with a microfibre cloth, then finish the clean visor with the Detailer.
conversation.speaker: seller

conversation.text: I have a matte helmet. Will the Detailer make the surface shiny?
conversation.speaker: client

conversation.text: Yes, it can be used on a matte helmet—the finish remains matte. Apply the product to a clean microfibre cloth and follow the helmet instructions.
conversation.speaker: seller

conversation.text: How long should I wait after applying the gel?
conversation.speaker: client

conversation.text: Follow the time stated on the label; the travel size specifies about 5 minutes. Do not let the product dry, and shorten the wait in direct sunlight.
conversation.speaker: seller

conversation.text: Can I use a paper towel?
conversation.speaker: client

conversation.text: Use a clean, soft microfibre cloth. Paper can be rough and may scratch a delicate surface.
conversation.speaker: seller

lessons.title: How to clean the visor and Pinlock correctly
lessons.summary: Learn how to clean the outside of a visor safely and distinguish it from the delicate Pinlock insert.

content.text: First identify which surface you are cleaning
The outer visor and Pinlock insert require different care. Before using any product, check the instructions for the specific helmet, visor and its coating.
Outer visor: gentle cleaning step by step
Remove loose sand and other particles without rubbing. Do not polish dirt while the surface is dry.
Apply Helmet Gel to dried-on insects and let it work as directed on the label. Do not let it dry.
Wipe away softened dirt with a clean cloth without pressing hard.
If the visor instructions allow it, use Helmet Detailer and a clean Evolon cloth for the final finish.
Pinlock: a separate, delicate insert
Do not use Helmet Gel or Helmet Detailer on the insert. Do not polish it with a cloth. Rinse it with distilled water without rubbing and leave it to air-dry.
What these products do not do
These products are for cleaning and finishing. They do not remove scratches or repair a damaged visor.

product_bullets: Remove loose sand without rubbing before you start cleaning the visor.
Apply gel to dried-on insects on the outside of the visor and wipe the dirt away without pressure.
Finish a clean outer visor with the Detailer and an Evolon cloth.
Do not apply gel or Detailer to the Pinlock, and do not polish it with a microfibre cloth.
Rinse the Pinlock with distilled water and leave it to air-dry.

conversation.text: Can I clean the Pinlock with the same product as the outer visor?
conversation.speaker: client

conversation.text: No. Use Helmet Gel and Detailer on the outside of the visor. Clean the Pinlock gently with distilled water, without rubbing, and follow the helmet instructions.
conversation.speaker: seller

conversation.text: There is sand on the visor. Can I wipe it with a microfibre cloth straight away?
conversation.speaker: client

conversation.text: First rinse it or gently remove the loose particles. Do not rub sand across the visor, as it may scratch it.
conversation.speaker: seller

conversation.text: Will these products remove scratches?
conversation.speaker: client

conversation.text: No. They are for cleaning and finishing, and will not repair scratches.
conversation.speaker: seller

lessons.title: How to care for the helmet interior
lessons.summary: Distinguish between freshening up the helmet interior and washing a dirty lining.

content.text: First identify the need

Ask whether the customer wants to freshen the interior after a ride or whether the lining is visibly dirty. A freshener and washing solve different problems: the product helps maintain freshness, while a dirty lining needs proper cleaning.
Freshen between washes
Mint freshener is designed for the inside of a helmet. Spray it from about 15–20 cm away and let the helmet dry completely before wearing it. The product is not intended for use on skin or the body.
Washing the lining

First check whether the lining can be removed and review the helmet manufacturer’s recommendations. For hand-washing, use a dedicated detergent according to its label. Wash gently, rinse thoroughly and leave it to air-dry. Do not wring the material or dry it near a heat source.
When to revisit the issue
If the smell persists after freshening, check the condition of the lining and consider washing it. Present the freshener as a complement to care between washes.

product_bullets: Ask whether the customer is concerned about odour or whether the dirty lining needs washing.
Mint freshener helps keep the helmet fresh between washes, but does not replace washing.
Spray the inside from about 15–20 cm away and wait until it is completely dry.
Hand-wash removable lining according to the helmet instructions.
Rinse thoroughly and air-dry; do not wring it or use a heat source.

conversation.text: The inside of the helmet smells of sweat. What should I choose?

conversation.text: Choose Mint to quickly freshen the helmet between washes. If the lining is dirty, wash it with a separate product according to the helmet instructions.
conversation.speaker: seller

conversation.text: Can I spray the product on my head?
conversation.speaker: client

conversation.text: No. Use it on the inside of the helmet as directed on the label, not on your skin.
conversation.speaker: seller

conversation.text: Can I put the helmet on straight after using it?
conversation.speaker: client

conversation.text: Wait until the inside is completely dry. If the smell returns, the lining may need washing.
conversation.speaker: seller

lessons.title: Which kit should you recommend: GIGA or Trip Kit?
lessons.summary: Choose Trip Kit or GIGA based on where and how often the customer cleans their helmet.

content.text: Choose the kit to suit how it will be used
Trip Kit and GIGA cover the steps for cleaning the outside of a helmet: softening dirt with gel, then finishing with the Detailer. They mainly differ in bottle size and ease of storage.
Trip Kit: for travelling
Compact bottles and a travel pouch make it easy to take the kit on a trip, store it in a case or compartment, and use it quickly during a stop.
GIGA: for regular care
The larger 250 ml bottles of gel and Detailer are suitable for frequent cleaning at home or in the garage, for example when caring for several helmets.
Questions that make choosing easier
Where will the helmet usually be cleaned—in the middle of a trip or at home?
How often will the customer clean it?
One helmet or several?
Is only the insect-removal step needed, or a final finish as well?
If the customer is concerned about an odour inside the helmet, discuss a separate interior product. A kit for cleaning the outside does not replace washing the lining.

product_bullets: Trip Kit and GIGA are for two-step cleaning of the outside of a helmet.
Trip Kit has compact bottles and a pouch, making it suitable for travel.
GIGA includes 250 ml bottles and accessories for regular use at home or in the garage.
Choose a separate product to freshen the interior—the outer-surface kits do not replace it.
Ask where and how often the customer will clean the helmet; do not assume the larger kit is better.

conversation.speaker: seller

conversation.text: Would Trip Kit be better for regularly cleaning two helmets at home?

conversation.speaker: client

lessons.title: Sales role-play: a customer is buying a new helmet
lessons.summary: Practise identifying needs and recommending care for a customer buying a helmet.

content.text: Exercise objective

Practise a conversation that helps someone buying a new helmet choose care products that suit their riding habits. Do not start with a list of products. Find out where and how often they will clean the helmet and what problem they want to solve.
What to focus on
Ask at least one question to help choose the right size.
Explain what the gel and Detailer do in two short sentences.
Do not recommend an add-on the customer does not need.
Do not promise a specific yield without verified data.
Individual practice

After acting out the scenarios, put the suggested answer into your own words. Finish by asking one question: “Do you clean your helmet more often on the road or at home?”, “One helmet or several?”, or “Are you mainly dealing with insects, or would you also like to freshen the interior?” Explain your recommendation in one sentence.

product_bullets: Start by asking where and how often the helmet will be cleaned, and how many helmets need care.
Choose Trip Kit for care on the road and GIGA for regular use at home.
Briefly explain the order: the gel softens dirt, and the Detailer finishes the clean surface.
Do not recommend an interior freshener if the customer does not need one.
Respect a refusal and do not promise a yield that has not been verified.

conversation.text: I’m going on a week-long trip and don’t want insects on my visor. What should I take?
conversation.speaker: client

conversation.text: For cleaning on the road, I recommend Trip Kit. The gel softens insects, and after you gently remove them, the Detailer helps finish the clean visor.
conversation.speaker: seller

conversation.text: Can I clean the Pinlock with the same kit?
conversation.speaker: client

conversation.text: Do not use products for the outer visor on the insert. Clean the Pinlock gently according to the manufacturer’s instructions.
conversation.speaker: seller

conversation.text: I don’t need anything for the interior; the helmet is new.
conversation.speaker: client

conversation.text: That’s fine—you do not need to buy a freshener just in case. You can come back to it if an odour or dirt becomes an issue.
conversation.speaker: seller

lessons.title: Why does motorcycle leather need care?
lessons.summary: Identify the type of leather and the dirt, then choose separate products for cleaning and conditioning.

content.text: First identify what you are dealing with

A leather suit may include different types of leather, colours, finishes and textile panels. Ask what exactly needs care, how heavy the dirt is, and whether the customer knows the manufacturer’s recommendations. Light-coloured or fluorescent leather requires extra care.
Separate cleaning from conditioning

Leather Cleaner removes dirt. Leather Milk is applied only to clean, dry leather to condition it. One product does not automatically replace the other, and care products do not repair physical damage.
Demonstrate the safe order
Remove loose dust without rubbing hard.
Test the product on a hidden area and check the result.
Clean gently with the appropriate cleaner and a soft brush.
Wipe away any residue with a clean, slightly damp cloth and leave it to air-dry.
If the leather needs conditioning, apply a thin layer of Leather Milk as directed on the label.
Set realistic expectations

A care product can clean and support routine maintenance, but it will not restore a worn finish or repair cracks. For this kind of damage, recommend having the garment assessed by a repair service or the manufacturer.

product_bullets: First identify the leather type and colour, and check the garment manufacturer’s recommendations.
Leather Cleaner removes dirt; Leather Milk conditions leather after it has dried.
Test the product on an inconspicuous area before use, especially on light-coloured leather.
Use a soft brush and light pressure for cleaning.
Care products cannot repair cracks, scuffs or damage to the finish.

conversation.text: I have a leather suit with bright-coloured panels. How should I start cleaning it?
conversation.speaker: client

conversation.text: For everyday dirt, choose Leather Cleaner Normal. For fluorescent colours, first test it on an inconspicuous area and clean with a soft brush.
conversation.speaker: seller

conversation.text: Is the leather conditioned after using the cleaner?
conversation.speaker: client

conversation.text: The cleaner removes dirt. Once the leather has dried completely, you can apply Leather Milk as a separate conditioning step.
conversation.speaker: seller

conversation.text: There is a crack near the seam. Will the milk repair it?
conversation.speaker: client

conversation.text: No. Care products condition leather but do not repair cracks or damaged seams. Take the garment to a repair service for this.
conversation.speaker: seller

lessons.title: How to clean leather: Leather Cleaner and a brush
lessons.summary: Choose the Leather Cleaner variant to suit the dirt and leather colour, then demonstrate a gentle cleaning technique.

content.text: Choose the variant to suit the leather and dirt

Do not automatically choose the strongest cleaner. Normal is suitable for everyday dirt and more delicate colours. Strong may be considered for heavier dirt on traditional leather, if the garment manufacturer’s instructions allow it.
Demonstration step by step
Shake the bottle and test the product on an inconspicuous area.
Apply the foam to a soft, slightly damp brush, not directly to the whole garment.
Clean a small area using calm, gentle strokes.
Wipe away the dirt with a clean, slightly damp cloth.
Leave the garment to air-dry before continuing with care.
When to change the approach
If the material has an unusual finish, a vivid colour or signs of damage, pause the demonstration and check the garment instructions. The cleaner removes dirt but does not repair scuffs or cracks.

product_bullets: Normal is the choice for everyday dirt and more delicate colours.
Consider Strong for heavier dirt on traditional leather after testing it first.
Shake the bottle and test the product on a hidden area.
Apply the foam to a soft, slightly damp brush; do not scrub hard.
Wipe away any residue and leave the leather to air-dry.

conversation.text: I have a white suit with fluorescent panels. Should I choose Strong?
conversation.speaker: client

conversation.text: For fluorescent colours, choose Normal and test it on a hidden area first. Reserve Strong for heavy dirt and use it only as intended.
conversation.speaker: seller

conversation.text: Can I use a hard shoe brush?
conversation.speaker: client

conversation.text: It is better to use a soft brush. Apply the foam to slightly damp bristles and gently clean a small area using circular motions.
conversation.speaker: seller

conversation.text: When should I apply Leather Milk?
conversation.speaker: client

conversation.text: After cleaning, wipe away the dirt with a clean cloth and let the leather air-dry. Apply the milk only to the dry surface, if it needs conditioning.
conversation.speaker: seller

lessons.title: How to condition leather: Leather Milk
lessons.summary: Explain Leather Milk as a conditioning step after the leather has been cleaned and dried.

content.text: Why condition leather

After cleaning and drying, leather may need separate conditioning. Leather Milk comes after the cleaner; it is not a detergent for dirty clothing. Explain this order to the customer before demonstrating how to apply it.
Apply without overdoing it
Make sure the leather is clean and completely dry.
Test it on an inconspicuous area, especially if the finish is unusual.
Apply a small amount of product with a soft cloth.
Spread it thinly and evenly, as directed on the label.
Leave it to dry and check the result before applying more.
What it can and cannot do

The milk supports routine care but does not repair cracks, scuffs or a damaged finish. Do not promise waterproofing unless the product manufacturer states that it provides it. If in doubt, refer to the garment instructions.

product_bullets: Apply Leather Milk to clean, dry leather.
Apply a thin, even layer as directed.
Test it on a hidden area before applying it to the whole garment.
Do not use the milk to remove dirt.
Do not promise that it will repair cracks or restore the original protective finish.

conversation.text: Why do I need Leather Milk if I already have Leather Cleaner?

conversation.speaker: seller

conversation.text: Can I apply the milk to a dirty jacket?
conversation.speaker: client

conversation.text: Clean and dry it first. The milk does not replace the cleaner.
conversation.speaker: seller

conversation.text: I have matte leather. How can I check whether the milk is suitable?
conversation.speaker: client

conversation.text: Test it on an inconspicuous area and check the garment manufacturer’s recommendations. Only then apply a thin layer as directed on the label.
conversation.speaker: seller

conversation.text: Will the milk repair cracks?
conversation.speaker: client

conversation.text: No. Cracks and scuffs need repair, not a care product.
conversation.speaker: seller

lessons.title: How to use the Leather Care Kit
lessons.summary: Guide the customer through the leather-care routine and check that each item meets a real need.

content.text: The kit as a step-by-step routine

Leather Care Kit can be convenient for someone who wants to care for the outside of leather garments and freshen their interior. The kit includes a cleaner, Leather Milk, an interior freshener, a brush and a cloth. Show the order of use instead of simply listing the items.
Order of use
Choose the cleaner variant to suit the dirt and colour, then test it.
Clean the leather with a soft brush and wipe away any residue.
Leave the leather to air-dry.
Apply a thin layer of Leather Milk as directed on the label.
Freshen the interior separately, following the instructions for that product.
Recommend the kit only when it fits

Ask what the customer already owns and whether they also need to care for the interior. If they have a cleaner and only need a conditioner, recommend just the missing step. Do not present the kit as essential for everyone.

product_bullets: Leather Care Kit combines a cleaner, conditioning milk, an interior freshener and accessories.
Clean the leather first, let it dry, then apply Leather Milk.
An interior freshener addresses a different need from care for the outside.
Choose Normal or Strong according to the colour, dirt and garment instructions.
If the customer already owns some of the products, recommend only what is missing.

conversation.text: My suit is dirty on the outside and smells inside. Will the kit solve both problems?
conversation.speaker: client

conversation.text: Leather Care Kit combines a cleaner, conditioning milk, an interior freshener and accessories. First clean the leather; once it dries, condition it with the milk, and freshen the interior separately.

conversation.text: I already have a cleaner. Is it still worth getting the whole kit?

conversation.text: The leather is cracked. Will the kit restore it?
conversation.speaker: client

conversation.text: It will not repair the damage. If the leather is cracked, consult a repair service first.
conversation.speaker: seller

lessons.title: Sales role-play: a customer is buying leather clothing
lessons.summary: Practise identifying the type of leather, choosing the simplest suitable solution and responding to the customer’s needs.

content.text: Start the conversation with a needs assessment

The aim of the role-play is to choose a solution for a specific suit, not to sell every product on the shelf. Find out the colour and type of leather, how dirty it is, its condition and what the customer already owns. Only then explain which steps are needed.
Three scenarios to practise
A light-coloured suit with fluorescent panels: choose the cleaner carefully and test it in a hidden area.
A heavily soiled black suit: choose a cleaner to suit the leather type, clean gently and let it dry.
A clean jacket that needs routine care: consider Leather Milk without adding an unnecessary cleaner.
Review together

After each conversation, the salesperson should be able to explain what is being purchased, in what order the products will be used and what they cannot repair. If the customer already owns some accessories, the recommendation may be limited to one missing product.

product_bullets: Ask about the type, colour and condition of the leather, as well as the garment manufacturer’s recommendations.
Separate cleaning the outer surface, conditioning it and freshening the interior.
Choose a cleaner to suit the colour and dirt; test it first on delicate leather.
Recommend Leather Milk after the leather has dried, if the customer needs conditioning.
Refer physical damage to a repair service; do not promise that a care product will repair it.

conversation.text: For fluorescent colours, choose Normal. Test it on an inconspicuous area, then clean a small section with a soft brush.
conversation.speaker: seller

conversation.text: I already have the cleaner. What do I need for care after cleaning?
conversation.speaker: client

conversation.text: If the leather needs it, choose Leather Milk on its own. Apply it only after the leather has dried following cleaning.
conversation.speaker: seller

conversation.text: There is a scuff on the sleeve. Will a care product hide it?
conversation.speaker: client

conversation.text: It smells of sweat inside. Should I wash the whole leather suit?
conversation.speaker: client

conversation.text: Do not start by soaking the suit. Choose a separate product for the interior and use it according to the garment instructions.

lessons.title: How to care for textile garments
lessons.summary: Identify the garment material and washing instructions, then choose the right product for the specific fibre.

content.text: Before choosing a detergent

Motorcycle clothing may combine a membrane, lining, armour and different fibres. Find out what the customer wants to wash, check the care label, and only then recommend a product. The garment instructions determine the temperature, programme, dosage and drying method.
Choose a product to suit the material
Textile Care: standard technical and membrane garments.
Active Care: synthetic sportswear, thermal base layers and microfibre.
Merino Care: merino wool and delicate natural fibres.
Jeans Care: denim, including motorcycle clothing when its care label allows it.
Fabric Protect: a laundry additive that helps maintain freshness, not a waterproofing treatment.
Do not wash everything the same way

A membrane jacket, thermal shirt and merino layer may require different detergents and wash programmes. Do not recommend fabric softener as a substitute for specialist care. If the customer wants to restore water repellency, choose a separate product for that purpose that is compatible with the garment instructions.

product_bullets: Start with the care label: material, temperature, programme, detergent and drying.
Choose Textile Care for technical clothing and Active Care for sportswear.
Merino Care is for delicate wool, while Jeans Care is for denim.
Fabric Protect helps maintain freshness during washing and is not a water-repellent treatment.
Wash different materials separately if they require different programmes and products.

conversation.text: It is better to separate them according to their care labels: they are different materials and may need different detergents and programmes. Choose Textile Care for the jacket and a separate product for the merino.

conversation.text: Will Fabric Protect waterproof my jacket?

conversation.text: I’m not sure which programme to use.

lessons.title: Textile Care: cleaning garments
lessons.summary: Explain what Textile Care is for and demonstrate how to choose it safely for technical garments.

content.text: What Textile Care is for

Textile Care is intended for technical motorcycle clothing, including garments with membranes. Do not promise that the detergent can repair a worn membrane or restore its properties after damage. The goal is to wash the garment correctly in line with its manufacturer’s instructions.
How to prepare for washing
Check the garment label and remove any items that need to be washed separately.
Select an approved programme and temperature.
Measure the detergent according to its label.
Do not add regular fabric softener unless the manufacturer explicitly recommends it.
Dry the garment as directed on the label, away from excessive heat if specified.
Extra freshness
Fabric Protect can be added to the wash as a separate additive. Explain its role clearly: it helps keep garments fresh but does not replace a water-repellent treatment.

product_bullets: Textile Care is designed for washing technical and membrane motorcycle clothing.
The garment label determines the programme, temperature and drying method.
Do not automatically substitute regular fabric softener.
Measure it according to the product label and washing instructions.
Fabric Protect can be considered as a separate additive to help maintain freshness.

conversation.text: Is Textile Care suitable for a membrane jacket?
conversation.speaker: client

conversation.text: Yes. It is a detergent for technical and membrane garments. Choose the programme and temperature according to the jacket’s care label.
conversation.speaker: seller

conversation.text: I always add fabric softener. Should I keep using it?
conversation.speaker: client

conversation.text: Do not automatically use it with technical clothing. Check the care label and use Textile Care as directed.
conversation.speaker: seller

conversation.text: What can I add if I want my clothes to smell fresh after washing?
conversation.speaker: client

conversation.text: You can add Fabric Protect to the fabric-softener compartment instead of regular softener, as directed on its label.
conversation.speaker: seller

lessons.title: Fabric Protect: care and freshness after washing
lessons.summary: Show how to add Fabric Protect to the wash and distinguish it from a waterproofing treatment.

content.text: A laundry additive, not a waterproofing treatment

The name may suggest water protection, so explain the product’s role clearly. Fabric Protect is an additive that helps maintain garment freshness during washing. It is not a water-repellent treatment and does not restore the DWR coating on its own.
How to use it
Choose a detergent that suits the material and check the garment label.
Pour Fabric Protect into the fabric-softener compartment if the instructions specify this.
Use the dosage stated on the label.
Select a programme that follows the garment instructions.
Use a separate product specifically intended for waterproofing.
How to explain the added value

If the customer washes technical clothing and wants it to stay fresh after washing, you can recommend Fabric Protect alongside Textile Care. If they ask about rain protection, explain clearly that they need a separate waterproofing treatment.

product_bullets: Fabric Protect is a laundry additive that helps maintain garment freshness.
It can replace regular fabric softener if the label says so.
Pour it into the fabric-softener compartment as directed.
Choose it alongside the right detergent for the material.

lessons.title: Active Care: caring for sportswear
lessons.summary: Choose Active Care for synthetic sportswear and thermal base layers according to how they are used.

content.text: When to consider Active Care

Active Care is suitable for synthetic sportswear, thermal base layers and microfibre. Start by asking about the customer’s activity and the issue they are trying to solve, such as odour after a workout or frequent washing of a base layer.
Match it to the material

If the customer asks about a membrane jacket, check its label and consider Textile Care. For merino wool, choose a product intended for delicate natural fibres. Do not choose Active Care just because the garment is sportswear.
Use and size

Always check the garment label for programme, temperature and drying instructions. Follow the product label for dosage. The 40 ml sachet can be a convenient option for trying the product or taking it on a trip.

product_bullets: Choose Active Care for synthetic sportswear and thermal base layers.
Ask about the material, odour after exercise and care-label instructions.
Do not assume that it is a detergent for every type of garment.
Follow the dosage and programme shown on the product and garment labels.
The 40 ml sachet lets the customer try the product before buying a larger size.

lessons.title: Merino Care
lessons.summary: Learn how to wash merino and delicate fibres, and avoid making overly broad recommendations.

content.text: Delicate fibres need special care

Merino layers help regulate comfort while riding and need to be cared for according to their labels. Merino Care is intended for merino wool and other delicate fibres specified by the manufacturer. Do not assume that a programme suitable for synthetic base layers is safe for wool.
Washing and drying
Check the fabric composition and care symbols on the label.
Choose a wool programme or hand-wash if specified.
Measure the detergent according to its label; for a small load, the label may specify 15–30 ml.
Avoid regular fabric softener unless the manufacturer recommends otherwise.
Air-dry the garment and do not place it on a hot radiator.
Sales conversation
Ask whether the customer is washing a merino layer on its own or a mixed-material garment. With mixed fabrics, separate washes may be better than using one detergent for everything.

product_bullets: Merino Care is intended for merino wool and delicate natural fibres.
Choose the temperature and programme primarily according to the garment label.
Use the detergent dosage stated on its label.
Do not add regular fabric softener unless it is explicitly recommended.
Air-dry as directed, away from excessive heat.

lessons.title: Jeans Care

content.text: Motorcycle denim is not always ordinary jeans

Care step by step

Remove the armour if the manufacturer allows it.
Choose Jeans Care for denim and follow the label for dosage.
Select the programme stated on the care label.

Choose a product that suits the garment

product_bullets: Choose Jeans Care for denim, including motorcycle clothing when its care label allows it.

lessons.title: Sales role-play: choosing care for different garment types

lessons.title: How to care for motorcycle gloves
lessons.summary: Identify whether the issue is on the inside or outside of the glove and choose the right care method.

content.text: First identify the problem

Gloves combine leather, textiles, armour, seams and hard-to-reach fingers. Ask whether the customer wants to remove dirt from the outside, freshen the inside or condition dry leather. These needs call for different solutions.
Check the glove instructions

Not every pair can be machine-washed or turned inside out. It is especially important to check the manufacturer’s recommendations for leather gloves. Do not soak or stretch them unless the instructions say to.
Choose the right care
Odour inside that is difficult to remove: consider Magiczne Rękawiczki and follow their instructions.
Dirt on the outside: choose a product to suit the glove material and manufacturer’s recommendations.
A zip is stiff but not damaged: consider Zip Service.
Scuffs, delamination and broken seams: a care product cannot replace a repair.
A concise recommendation
When recommending a product, explain what it is for and what it cannot do. Magiczne Rękawiczki freshen the inside; they do not fully wash or repair the glove.

product_bullets: Gloves have seams, armour and different materials, so check the care label.
Distinguish dirt on the outside from odour or moisture inside.
Do not assume that gloves can be machine-washed or turned inside out.
Magiczne Rękawiczki help freshen hard-to-reach areas inside.
Damaged or delaminated seams and scuffed leather need professional repair.

lessons.title: Magiczne Rękawiczki: use and demonstration
lessons.summary: Show the customer how to use Magiczne Rękawiczki to freshen the inside of their gloves.

content.text: Why use Magiczne Rękawiczki

The impregnated pair makes it easier to clean hard-to-reach areas inside gloves that cannot easily be turned inside out. This can be especially useful for leather gloves if their instructions allow this method of freshening.
Demonstration
Open the sachet and put the single-use pair on your hands.
Put your hands inside the motorcycle gloves.
Move your fingers and apply gentle pressure so the product reaches the inside.
Do not pull at the lining or force the glove inside out.
When finished, remove the impregnated pair and wash your hands as directed.
What not to promise

This is a practical way to freshen the inside, not a substitute for washing the whole glove, repairing seams or removing every type of dirt. The customer should use the product as directed on the packaging.

product_bullets: The sachet contains one pair of impregnated, single-use gloves.
Put them on your hands, place your hands inside the motorcycle gloves and move your fingers.
Work gently to reach the inside without turning the glove inside out.
This is a way to freshen the inside, not to fully wash or repair the gloves.
After use, remove the product and wash your hands as directed.

Wipe away any excess with a clean, dry cloth.

An add-on product
You can recommend it as a practical add-on for clothing, footwear or a bag if the customer mentions a zip problem. Do not promise that it will repair broken teeth, torn fabric or a damaged slider.

product_bullets: Zip Service helps working metal and plastic zips slide more smoothly.
Apply a small amount to the teeth and move the slider back and forth several times.
Wipe away excess with a clean, dry cloth.
It can be useful for zips on clothing, footwear and bags.
It will not repair broken teeth or a damaged slider.

lessons.title: Where to start with motorcycle care
lessons.summary: Identify the type of dirt and choose a simple motorcycle-care routine.

content.text: Start with an assessment

A motorcycle after a dry ride needs a different approach from one ridden in the rain or through mud. Ask what kind of dirt is present, how heavy it is, and whether the customer has access to water, a pressure washer and a garage. This helps you recommend a simple sequence instead of a random collection of products.
Quick refresh
For light dust between full washes, Wash & Ride and a clean, soft microfibre cloth may be enough. Do not use this method to rub off coarse sand, which can scratch the paint.
Full wash
Consider Bug Killer as a pre-wash step for dried-on insects.
Use Moto Wash or a prepared Power Powder solution for the main wash.
For deposits on the wheels, choose Wheelixir and the right accessory.
Rinse and dry the motorcycle according to the product instructions.
You can apply Ceramic Detailer as a finishing step to a clean, cool surface.
Explain the limitations
Do not apply products to hot components or let them dry on the surface if the instructions warn against this. Ceramic Detailer does not replace washing or a professional, long-lasting coating.

product_bullets: Identify dust, insects, brake dust, grease or heavy mud.
Ask about access to water and the cleaning conditions.
Wash & Ride is suitable for light dust between full washes.
Bug Killer, Moto Wash and Wheelixir are for different steps and types of dirt.
Use Ceramic Detailer after washing, on a clean, cool surface.

lessons.title: Wash & Ride: motorcycle cleaning

content.text: Quick cleaning without a hose

Wash & Ride is convenient when a motorcycle needs a light refresh and the customer has no access to a hose or bucket. It complements regular washing; it is not a substitute when there is a thick layer of mud, sand or heavy deposits.
How to use it
Make sure the surface is cool.
Spray the product onto a small area as directed on the label.
Gently wipe away the dirt with a clean, soft microfibre cloth; do not press hard.
Turn the cloth to a clean side or replace it when it picks up dirt.
For heavy dirt, stop and plan a full wash.
Who it is for
The product is useful between washes in the garage, in a car park or on the road. It helps refresh the appearance and leaves a light protective layer as stated by the product manufacturer.

product_bullets: Wash & Ride is for dust and light dirt between full washes.
Use it on a cool surface and gently wipe away dirt with a clean microfibre cloth.
It can be useful in a garage, car park or while travelling.
Do not use it to rub off a thick layer of sand or mud.
For heavy dirt, rinse the motorcycle and carry out a full wash.

Bug Killer and Wheelixir are separate concentrates for different purposes.

Bug Killer is for pre-treating insects, bird droppings and other organic dirt. Wheelixir is for deposits on wheels and around the brake calipers. Neither replaces washing the entire motorcycle.

If there are insects on the fairing, recommend a product for organic dirt. If dark deposits are on the wheel, choose a wheel cleaner. Check compatibility and work on a cool surface.

lessons.title: Ceramic Detailer: finishing and protection

content.text: The finishing step after washing

Set clear expectations
The Detailer can support routine care and help reduce dirt adhesion. The motorcycle still needs washing, and the product does not replace a durable coating or paint restoration.

lessons.title: Brushes and microfibre cloths: choosing accessories
lessons.summary: Choose a microfibre cloth and brush for each step, and avoid transferring dirt between surfaces.

Even a good product cannot replace the right tool. A soft microfibre cloth removes light dirt and is used for finishing. Choose separate brushes for wheels, the chain and hard-to-reach details.

lessons.title: What kinds of dirt build up during off-road riding?
lessons.summary: Identify off-road dirt and choose Mud Breaker or Dirt Finisher to match its severity.

content.text: Why off-road riding needs a different approach

After an off-road ride, a motorcycle may be covered in mud, sand, dust and residue from puddles. Dry particles are abrasive, so do not start by wiping the whole bike with a microfibre cloth. First assess the amount of dirt and prepare for safe cleaning.
Choose one of two approaches
Thick, dried mud: use Mud Breaker as directed, then rinse thoroughly.
Light dust after a dry ride: Dirt Finisher and a clean microfibre cloth may be enough.
A lot of sand: remove it safely before wiping the surface.
Questions to ask before recommending

Ask what kind of terrain the customer rides on and whether they have access to water. Mud Breaker needs to be rinsed off. Do not promise that it will prevent future mud from sticking or make the motorcycle self-cleaning.

Do not wipe a thick layer of dry sand, as the particles can cause scratches.

lessons.title: Mud Breaker: removing mud

Wait for the motorcycle to cool down.

Apply the product to dirty components as directed on the label.

Rinse away the dirt and product thoroughly with water.

Use it on a dirty surface as directed on the label.

Rinse the vehicle thoroughly after the product has worked.

conversation.speaker: seller

conversation.text: I don’t have a hose. Should I use it in the car park?
conversation.speaker: client

conversation.text: Not unless you can rinse it off. Use Mud Breaker where water is available, because the vehicle must be rinsed thoroughly after it has worked.
conversation.speaker: seller

conversation.text: Can I leave the product to dry?
conversation.speaker: client

conversation.text: No. Rinse it off before it dries and do not apply it to hot components.
conversation.speaker: seller

lessons.title: Dirt Finisher: finishing and care
lessons.summary: Explain how Dirt Finisher is used for light dirt and as a step after a heavier wash.

content.text: Lighter care for off-road motorcycles

Dirt Finisher is not another version of Mud Breaker. It helps with light dirt and finishing a cleaner surface. For heavy mud, it is a follow-up step only after the dirt has been softened and rinsed away.
How to use it
Check that the surface is cool and free of thick sand.
Shake the bottle as directed.
Spray a small amount onto the chosen area.
Gently wipe away light dirt with a clean microfibre cloth.
Change the cloth when it picks up sand or mud.
Match it to the amount of dirt

Dirt Finisher may be enough on its own for light dust after riding on gravel. For a thick layer of clay, use Mud Breaker and rinse first. The finishing step can make later care easier, but it does not eliminate dirt.

product_bullets: Dirt Finisher is intended for light cleaning and finishing.
For heavy mud, use Mud Breaker first and rinse thoroughly.
Before use, remove coarse sand and check that the surface is cool.
Shake the bottle and work in small sections.
Wipe away dirt with a clean microfibre cloth and replace it when it becomes heavily soiled.

conversation.text: Do I need to buy Mud Breaker and Dirt Finisher together?
conversation.speaker: client

conversation.text: No. Dirt Finisher is enough for light dust. For heavy mud, use Mud Breaker first and rinse; add the finishing product only if you need it.
conversation.speaker: seller

conversation.text: Will Dirt Finisher handle a thick layer of clay?
conversation.speaker: client

conversation.text: No. First soften the mud with Mud Breaker and rinse it off. Dirt Finisher is for lighter cleaning and finishing.
conversation.speaker: seller

conversation.text: Can I wipe away a lot of sand with it?
conversation.speaker: client

conversation.text: Remove coarse sand first. Do not rub particles into the surface with a microfibre cloth, as they can scratch it.
conversation.speaker: seller

lessons.title: How to choose an Off-Road Kit
lessons.summary: Choose an off-road care kit to suit the riding style, amount of dirt and access to water.

content.text: Ask what the customer means by a “kit”

The customer may mean a ready-made package or a set of care products. Ask what they ride, what kind of dirt they encounter most often and whether they have access to water after a ride. Until you confirm a specific product, present the solution as a two-step system.
Tailor the recommendation to the rider
Motocross on a muddy track: Mud Breaker, rinsing and Dirt Finisher if needed.
Enduro on dry gravel: Dirt Finisher for light dust.
Quad or mountain bike in heavy mud: choose a product and check the vehicle’s care instructions.
No access to water: plan to clean where you can rinse the vehicle properly.
Accessories and choosing the essentials

A clean, soft microfibre cloth is useful for finishing, and a suitable brush can reach tight areas. Do not add products unnecessarily. First recommend the essentials that solve the problem, then present a second step as an option.

product_bullets: Find out whether the customer rides motocross, enduro, a quad or a mountain bike.
For heavy mud, recommend Mud Breaker and access to water for rinsing.
For light dust, the customer can start with Dirt Finisher.
Recommend an extra microfibre cloth or brush only if there is a real need.
Do not present Off-Road Kit as a specific ready-made package unless you have confirmed the product.

conversation.text: I want one enduro kit and don’t want five different liquids. What are the essentials?
conversation.speaker: client

conversation.text: If you most often deal with heavy mud and have water for rinsing, start with Mud Breaker. Add Dirt Finisher only if you also want to finish the clean surface.
conversation.speaker: seller

conversation.text: I mostly ride on dry gravel. Do I need both products?
conversation.speaker: client

conversation.text: No. For light dust, start with Dirt Finisher and a clean microfibre cloth.
conversation.speaker: seller

conversation.text: Is Off-Road Kit a ready-made box?
conversation.speaker: client

conversation.text: Let’s check which retail option is currently available. If you mean a care kit, I can recommend Mud Breaker and Dirt Finisher as two separate steps.
conversation.speaker: seller

lessons.title: How to identify a customer’s needs
lessons.summary: Ask questions that uncover the customer’s needs and lead to a simple recommendation.

content.text: Sales starts with listening

A customer may describe a problem without knowing product names: “I’m looking for something for my helmet” or “my jacket smells unpleasant.” Your task is to clarify what they need, not immediately list the available products.
Five helpful questions
What would you like to clean or protect?
What is the main issue: insects, dust, mud, sweat or conditioning?
What material is the garment or surface made from?
Where will you use the product, and will you have access to water?
Is this a one-off need or for regular care?
From answers to a recommendation

You do not need to ask every question. Choose the ones that affect which product is suitable. Restate the problem in your own words, recommend one solution, explain how to use it and mention an important limitation. Suggest an add-on only when it fills a specific gap in the process.

product_bullets: Ask what the customer wants to clean or protect.
Identify the specific issue: insects, dust, mud, odour or conditioning.
Check the material, conditions of use and how often it needs care.
Summarise the problem in your own words before recommending a product.
Present one or two suitable solutions and explain how to use them.

conversation.text: I need a good cleaning product. What do you recommend?
conversation.speaker: client

conversation.text: First, let’s find out what you want to clean: a helmet, clothing or a motorcycle. What problem are you trying to solve—insects, dirt, odour or material care?
conversation.speaker: seller

conversation.text: The customer asks only about the price straight away. What should I say?
conversation.speaker: client

conversation.text: Give the price if you know it, then briefly ask what they need it for. This helps you identify the right option without pushing an unnecessary product.
conversation.speaker: seller

lessons.title: How to recommend kits instead of individual products
lessons.summary: Show the value of a kit by explaining its care steps, and choose a size that suits how it will be used.

content.text: Explain the process, not just the price

A kit makes sense when the customer understands the steps it covers. For leather garments, these may include cleaning, conditioning and freshening the inside. For helmets, consider cleaning the outer surfaces and choosing a size that is convenient at home or on the road.
Choose a kit to suit the situation
Consider Leather Care Kit for someone who needs several steps for leather care.
Trip Kit is handy for travel.
GIGA can be convenient for regular care at home or for several helmets.
If the customer already has accessories, recommend only the missing product.
Check what the customer needs

A kit is not always the best choice. Ask what the customer already owns, how often they care for their gear and where they will use it. A kit’s value comes from convenience and suitability, not simply from the number of items.

product_bullets: Explain the process: cleaning, conditioning or finishing, and then the interior if relevant.
Leather Care Kit can combine care for outer leather with freshening the interior.
Trip Kit is suitable for travel; GIGA is for regular helmet care.
A customer who already owns some products can buy only what is missing.
Finish by asking how and how often the products will be used.

conversation.text: Why do I need a kit if I only need one product?
conversation.speaker: client

conversation.text: If you already have the other products and accessories, buy only the product you are missing. A kit makes sense when you want to complete every step of the care routine.
conversation.speaker: seller

conversation.text: I need something for my helmet while travelling. What should I choose?
conversation.speaker: client

conversation.text: Choose Trip Kit—it has compact bottles that are easy to take on the road. For regular cleaning at home, compare it with GIGA.
conversation.speaker: seller

conversation.text: Does the larger kit work better?
conversation.speaker: client

conversation.text: No, the kits differ in size and contents. Choose according to how often you clean and how many helmets you have.
conversation.speaker: seller

lessons.title: How to increase sales with complementary products
lessons.summary: Recommend at most one relevant complementary product to support the care process the customer is already starting.

content.text: Good complementary selling

An add-on is valuable when it completes another step in the process. A customer buying a cleaner may also need a product for follow-up conditioning or a suitable cloth. If they already own that item, there is no reason to recommend it again.
Natural product pairings
Helmet Gel → Helmet Detailer and a suitable cloth.
Leather Cleaner → Leather Milk after the leather has been cleaned and dried.
Textile Care → Fabric Protect as an additive for freshness, not waterproofing.
Moto Wash or Bug Killer → Ceramic Detailer after washing and rinsing.
Mud Breaker → Dirt Finisher after a heavy wash if the customer wants a finishing step.
Recommend without pressure

Ask what step is missing and offer no more than one relevant add-on. For example: “The cleaner will remove dirt from the leather. If you do not have a product for conditioning it after cleaning, I can show you Leather Milk.” If the customer declines, respect their decision.

product_bullets: An add-on should support the next care step, not simply increase the basket.
Helmet Gel can be paired with the Detailer and a suitable cloth.
Leather Milk complements Leather Cleaner once the leather has dried.
Textile Care can be paired with Fabric Protect as a laundry additive.
Respect a refusal and do not recommend a product that duplicates what the customer already owns.

lessons.title: How to respond to common customer objections
lessons.summary: Respond to objections by understanding the concern, sharing a relevant fact and leaving the decision to the customer.

content.text: An objection provides information

“It’s too expensive,” “I already have something similar” or “Is it safe?” are signs that the customer needs clarification. First acknowledge their concern, then ask a brief question, give a factual answer and leave the choice to them.
Four common situations
Price: ask whether the product will be used occasionally or regularly, then choose the right size.
Regular detergent: compare its intended use with the material and garment label.
Safety: check the surface, finish and instructions; test the product first on leather.
Effectiveness: explain the product’s specific function and limitations.
Answer in three sentences

A brief response can acknowledge the concern, share a specific fact and suggest a next step. Do not scare the customer with potential damage, promise that a product works “for everything” or invent a returns policy. If you do not know the answer, check it before making a recommendation.
Practice

In pairs, practise responding to these objections: “It’s too expensive,” “I already have regular detergent,” “Is it safe?” and “Will it work?” Swap roles and check that your answer stays within the product’s intended use.

product_bullets: First acknowledge the concern and ask a clarifying question.
When discussing price, choose a size and contents to suit how often it will be used.
For safety, check the surface, care label and manufacturer’s recommendations.
Explain what the product is for instead of making broad promises.
Do not make claims about returns, repairs or results that you cannot verify.

conversation.text: That is too expensive for me.
conversation.speaker: client

conversation.text: I understand. If you will use it occasionally, let’s look at a smaller size or buy only the product you need for this step.
conversation.speaker: seller

conversation.text: Is this product safe for every material?
conversation.speaker: client

conversation.text: There is no single product for everything. Tell me what material you need it for, and I’ll choose a product and method that follow its care label.

conversation.speaker: client

conversation.text: Let’s compare the size, variant and kit contents. If it is the same product, you can choose whichever offer suits you better.
conversation.speaker: seller

lessons.title: Sales conversation role-plays
lessons.summary: Practise complete sales conversations, from identifying a need to choosing one suitable solution.

content.text: Scenario: a helmet after a ride

The customer has bought their first helmet and has dried-on insects on the visor. Ask whether they clean it at home or on the road. Explain how to soften the dirt and then finish the clean surface. If they ask about Pinlock, distinguish the insert from the outer visor and follow the manufacturer’s instructions.
Scenario: a suit after the season

The customer has dirty leather and an odour inside the suit. Separate cleaning the exterior, conditioning after it dries and freshening the interior. If they already own a cleaner, recommend only the missing step. Refer a scuff in the material to a repair service.
Scenario: an enduro bike after riding in mud

The customer returns from a demanding off-road ride and has access to water. Recommend Mud Breaker and thorough rinsing; present Dirt Finisher as an optional finishing step. Do not recommend wiping dry sand or applying products to hot components.
Conversation recap

In every scenario, identify the need, recommend a suitable product, and explain how to use it and its limitations. Leave the decision to the customer, and if no add-on is needed, finish with the basic solution.

product_bullets: Ask how the product will be used before presenting it.
Choose a product for the specific problem and material.
Explain the order of use and one important safety condition.
Recommend an add-on only if it fills a needed step.
If there is damage or you are unsure, check the instructions or refer the customer to a repair service.
